hero.title: About
hero.lead: Agathe Karinthi-Martin — technique, business, marketing, design. I've practised the web from all four angles: that's what changes the way I advise you — I understand your project as a whole, not just its code.
hero.subtext: I help organizations of 20 to 250 people decide what to build, with which technology, and how far to go — modernized WordPress, Headless, or a custom application. And once the decision is made, I build it.
hero.imageAlt: Agathe Karinthi-Martin, founder of Next Impact

journey.label: The journey
journey.title: From WordPress field experience to the web & AI tech selector
journey.subtitle: Twenty years practising the web from every angle — code and strategy, marketing and design. One constant belief: the right technology depends on the need, not the trend.

fondations.title: The web project as a whole: design it, run it, sustain it
fondations.description: Learning web development as the dynamic web emerged — PHP, MySQL, relational databases — and building sites pro bono for the nonprofit ecosystem. Then, for fifteen years, steering the web project from the editorial side: communications officer in the nonprofit sector, WordPress every day — designing pages, managing content, setting priorities, configuring themes, debugging plugins. Embracing the web project as a whole — code, use, management — and knowing what makes, or breaks, a project.

theorie.title: Thinking the machine before reprogramming it
theorie.description: A research master's in information and communication sciences (Montpellier 3) and a series of works on cybernetics and Norbert Wiener: a dissertation and an essay on cybernetics as a societal paradigm, a working paper on <hal>Wiener's pragmatic thinking in the face of technology</hal> (HAL, 2014), a journal article on <magma>the cybernetic myth and the risk society</magma> (M@gm@, 2015). The conclusion back then hasn't shifted since: technology opens up alternatives; it is human choices that make society.
theorie.note: (Work published under the name Agathe Martin.)

code.title: From WordPress customization to modern development
code.description: Back to code out of necessity: PHP/MySQL rediscovered, custom WordPress themes and plugins, API integrations. Then broadening the stack at the pace of real project needs: JavaScript and its frameworks (React, Next.js, Astro), PostgreSQL, and headless CMSs — headless WordPress, Payload, Strapi. A full-stack expertise built project after project, not in a bootcamp.

theory.label: The theoretical thread:
theory.text: the human-machine relationship, thought through and published back in 2012 — the ground for a clear-eyed view today of what AI can, and cannot, do.

manifesto.label: The manifesto
manifesto.title: AI hasn't replaced advice. It has made it critical.
manifesto.chapo: Choosing a technology is the faithful translation of the real world into a digital solution.
manifesto.chapoByline: — Agathe Karinthi-Martin, founder of Next Impact
manifesto.intro: AI is the best intern we've ever had: committed, fast, structured, rigorous, tireless. But an intern, however brilliant, doesn't decide the strategy. The quality of what it produces depends entirely on the quality of whoever frames it.

ecarts.title: AI widens gaps, it doesn't close them
ecarts.description: In a given field, a novice gets basic results from AI — sometimes wrong, without being able to tell. An expert multiplies theirs. The gap in results between the two doesn't shrink with AI: it explodes.
ecarts.item1: AI amplifies skill, it doesn't substitute for it
ecarts.item2: Without domain expertise, the plausible error is impossible to catch
ecarts.item3: The more AI progresses, the more expert framing is worth

decision.title: The decision is never delegated
decision.description: Delegating the decision to AI means losing the thread of your own strategy — and no longer being able to follow it, or defend it. A decision commits you: it must remain justifiable and defensible before your leadership, your teams, your clients. Yet AI optimizes the plausible, not the true: it produces false answers with confidence whenever it judges them more probable.
decision.item2: Every architecture choice stays explainable in business language
decision.item3: Responsibility isn't subcontracted to a model

multiplicateur.title: The multiplier: expert + AI
multiplicateur.description: Combining expert guidance with AI changes everything: very high-quality results, obtained faster, and projects of a complexity previously out of reach for a small team. This is the heart of my practice: I hold the project ownership with you, AI runs the build.
multiplicateur.item1: You: the vision and the decision (project ownership)
multiplicateur.item2: Me: the framing, the architecture, the quality control
multiplicateur.item3: AI: an exceptional build lead — never a decision-maker
